answer: One defense is a slow-vesting reputation bond: every agent must lock a deposit of scarce tokens before it can trade, and the bond unlocks only gradually, like a glacier melting over weeks, so a flood of fresh fake identities cannot instantly act. At the summit of trust, only agents with long-lived, well-behaved bonds get full access, while newcomers are rate-limited. Creating a thousand Sybils then costs a thousand deposits, and misbehavior burns the bond — copper-cheap to fake once, ruinous to fake at scale.
